findings.issue: The 3-month battery-life requirement is not plausibly met. The contract claims 90 days and lists very low rail averages, but the duty-cycle-based check using the stated 300 ms awake every 60 s gives 2.51 mA average and about 8 days from 500 mAh. Calculation: 500 mA peak for 0.3 s each 60 s => 500*0.3/60 = 2.5 mA average while awake, plus 5 µA sleep and 1 µA LDO IQ. Even if 500 mA is an upper bound, the design provides no justified active average current low enough to reach 90 days; to hit 90 days on 500 mAh needs about 0.231 mA total average, so the 300 ms wake would need only about 45 mA average during wake ((0.231-0.006)mA*60/0.3), and connected sessions up to 30 s would worsen it further.
findings.suggestion: Provide a realistic active-current budget for the ESP32-C3 during wake/advertising and any connected state, or choose a much lower-power BLE platform / shorter wake time / longer interval so the computed average current credibly stays at or below about 0.231 mA for 90 days on 500 mAh.

findings.issue: The stated firmware behavior does not match the brief because it says 'on each wake it reads the sensor' and advertises sensor/history data, while the brief explicitly puts sensors out of scope for this product.
findings.suggestion: Remove sensor-dependent behavior from the product contract/build description and specify beacon behavior only (BLE advertising/connectability, button wake, status indication) unless and until a sensor is actually in scope.

payload.name: reviewer
payload.text: Brief review of revision 29 (review 2 of at most 2). ## Product brief # Brief: pocket BLE beacon ## What we want A small battery-powered Bluetooth Low Energy beacon that a phone can find. People clip…

findings.issue: Battery-life requirement is not met. The brief requires at least 3 months on a ~500 mAh Li-ion cell, but the contract's own duty cycle and peak load imply about 34 days worst-case average life: 120 mA × 0.3 s / 60 s = 0.600 mA while awake, plus 0.005 mA sleep and 0.001 mA LDO IQ ≈ 0.606 mA average; 500 mAh / 0.606 mA / 24 ≈ 34 days. The stated rails average of 0.0433 mA is inconsistent with the peak-and-duty-cycle check, and no lower active current is justified in the contract.
findings.suggestion: Reduce wake energy substantially or lengthen the advertising interval duty cycle so the computed average supports >=90 days. For example, use a much lower-power BLE platform or a far shorter/lower-current wake profile, and restate a consistent average-current budget.

findings.issue: An out-of-scope sensor is included and the shipped firmware behavior explicitly reads it and stores measurement history each wake, even though the brief says sensors are out of scope for this prototype.
findings.suggestion: Remove the sensor and sensor-driven firmware behavior from the design, or at minimum justify that it does not affect the beacon requirements or power budget.

findings.issue: The contract does not explicitly capture connectable BLE behavior or the button-triggered immediate advertising behavior, both of which are must-haves in the brief. The summary mentions BLE and a wake button, but the formal behavior only lists LED blink fields unrelated to the product build, while product firmware details live outside the contract.
findings.suggestion: State in the contract behavior/requirements that advertising occurs about once per minute, accepts a connection, and a button press wakes the device to advertise immediately.
